old.name: Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfandel
old.label: RED
old.hook: Native red of Pelješac · Crljenak × Dobričić · UC Davis 1998 DNA proof
chips: Dinner, paired with brodet or peka
old.text: Native red of Pelješac · Crljenak × Dobričić · UC Davis 1998 DNA proof EUR 18–120 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner, paired with brodet or peka "Little blue" — the native red of Dalmatia. Prof. Carole Meredith at UC Davis in 1998 , with vine cuttings shipped by Mike Grgich himself, proved that Plavac Mali is the offspring of Crljenak Kaštelanski × Dobričić — and that Crljenak Kaštelanski is genetically identical to Zinfandel (California) and Primitivo (Apulia). So Croatia is the grandparent of California Zinfandel. The flagship appellations: Dingač (1961) and Postup (1967), both on Pelješac's south-facing slopes. Where Pelješac peninsula

old.name: Dingač — Croatia's first protected wine
old.label: APPELLATION 1961
old.hook: 1961 appellation · 45° slopes · grapes sun-cooked three times
old.text: 1961 appellation · 45° slopes · grapes sun-cooked three times EUR 28–80 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner Dingač was declared in 1961 — the first protected wine appellation in former Yugoslavia and modern Croatia. The vines grow on south-facing 45° slopes between Trstenik and Podobuče on the Pelješac peninsula, where the grapes are heat-cooked three ways at once: direct sun, sun reflected off the Adriatic, sun reflected off the white karst stones. Historically the grapes were brought down by donkey through a hand-dug path; since 1973 the ~400 m Dingač tunnel connects Potomje on the cooler north shore to the warm south. Drink at D'vino in a flight if you can't make Pelješac. Where Pelješac · Trstenik–Podobuče

old.name: Pošip — Korčula white
old.label: WHITE
old.hook: Native white of Korčula · first documented 1864 · first protected Croatian white (PGI 1967)
old.text: Native white of Korčula · first documented 1864 · first protected Croatian white (PGI 1967) EUR 14–55 / bottle ESSENTIAL Lunch with oysters; aperitivo Pošip is the white that pairs with Mali Ston oysters. Native to Korčula, grown almost exclusively in the Smokvičko-čarsko polje — the linked vineyards of Smokvica and Čara . First documented vine 1864 (Marin Tomašić of Čara); PGI status in 1967, the first protected white wine in Croatia . DNA work shows the grape is a natural cross of Bratovina × Blatska Zlatarica. Notes: citrus, salt, almond, the mouthfeel of a lower-acid Mediterranean white. Usually 13.5–14.5% abv. Try Krajančić , Bire , Toreta , or the Grgić Pošip. Where Korčula · Smokvica · Čara

old.name: Grk — only Lumbarda
old.label: SINGLE-VILLAGE
old.hook: Single-village white from sandy soils · ~2,400 years on the island · female-only vines
old.text: Single-village white from sandy soils · ~2,400 years on the island · female-only vines EUR 22–48 / bottle RARE Aperitivo or with crudo "The Greek" — white wine from a single village, Lumbarda on the eastern tip of Korčula. Planted by Greek colonists from Issa (Vis) in the 4th c. BCE . Grown in sandy soils that resisted phylloxera , which is why the vines are pre-phylloxera ungrafted. The genetic curiosity: Grk vines are female-only and must be co-planted with Plavac Mali to set fruit. Production is small — under 100 ha in total — and a chef can drink it nowhere in the Old Town except D'vino , who stocks the Bire and Lumbarda Vina bottlings. Where Korčula · Lumbarda

old.name: Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert wine
old.label: DESSERT WINE
old.hook: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine — name fight with Italian Prosecco (partially lost 2022)
chips: With dessert; a hit of it in pašticada marinade
old.text: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine — name fight with Italian Prosecco (partially lost 2022) EUR 18–60 / bottle ESSENTIAL FOR PAŠTICADA With dessert; a hit of it in pašticada marinade Prošek is the Dalmatian dessert wine — grapes sun-dried on straw mats for 2–3 weeks to concentrate sugars, then fermented slowly. Sweet, port-like, amber. Not Italian Prosecco : the Italian sparkling shares only the syllable. The EU-PDO arbitration of 2022 partially rejected Croatia's Prošek protection in favour of Italian Prosecco — a sore point on every Dalmatian dinner table. The dessert wine still gets called Prošek inside Croatia; it is also the soul of pašticada's marinade. Try Hectorovich from Hvar or Saints Hills Prošek . Where Dalmatian-wide

old.name: Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Rozalin
old.label: RAKIJA
old.hook: Herb / grape / walnut / rose-petal — the home rakija quartet
old.text: Herb / grape / walnut / rose-petal — the home rakija quartet EUR 3–6 / pour EVERYWHERE Aperitivo and digestif Travarica — clear grape rakija infused with sage, rosemary, fennel and immortelle; the aperitivo. Loza — the straight grape eau-de-vie of the coast. Orahovac — green-walnut liqueur: walnuts picked unripe around St John's Day, 24 June , steeped 40+ days in rakija with cloves, cinnamon and sugar — comes out dark amber and tastes Christmas-y. Rozalin / Rozulin — Dubrovnik-specific rose-petal liqueur, the perfume that makes a proper Rožata caramel taste of Dubrovnik and not of crème caramel elsewhere. Where Konavle agroturizam · home tables

old.name: Buža — the hole-in-the-wall bar
old.label: GEM
old.text: Two bars literally cut into the south sea wall — Buža means "hole." Walk past the cathedral down toward the wall, look for a small wooden door painted with "COLD DRINKS WITH THE MOST BEAUTIFUL VIEW." Tables on rocks above 10 m of water; swimmers jumping below. Drinks only — no food. Buža I and Buža II are run by different families; both honest. Beer + house white. Cash-only by tradition. Where Old Town · south sea wall When Daily 09:00 till after midnight in summer
